title: How tap-to-pay works

segments.text: How does tap to pay work?
Your payment card doesn't even have a battery.
Step one: a coil in the terminal creates a magnetic field that reaches just a few centimetres.
Step two: a loop antenna hidden in your card catches that field, and turns it into power for the chip.
To answer, the card doesn't transmit at all. It flickers how much power it draws, and the terminal reads the flicker.
Step three: for every payment, the chip creates a one-time code. Copy it, and it won't work again.
Phones go further: they don't even share your real card number, only a substitute called a token.
So the terminal powers your card for a moment, and your card pays with a code that only works once.

sources: https://www.emvco.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/EMV%C2%AE-Chip-At-A-Glance-EMVCo-eBook.pdf (EMVCo: 'For both contact and contactless payments, the acceptance terminal provides power to the chip'; contactless needs 'a maximum distance of a few centimetres'; chip 'generates a one-time use security code for every transaction'; EMV Payment Tokenisation for mobile devices 'replacing valuable card data in a transaction with a payment token')
https://www.emvco.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/EMVCo_QRG_EMV-CONTACTLESS_FINAL.pdf (EMVCo: 'A one-time use security code is generated for every transaction'; tokenisation for mobile devices)

https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/application-note/AN13453.pdf (NXP, chip maker: an ISO/IEC 14443 card is 'a passive device (without battery)' 'powered by magnetic field generated by a PCD', and 'requires a loop antenna')

https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/application-note/AN11706.pdf (NXP: the ISO/IEC 14443 reader antenna coil 'generates the magnetic field to provide the power to operate a card (PICC)', transmits to and receives from the card; the passive side 'uses the load modulation principle to send its data'; reader tests check the card's load-modulation response)

https://support.apple.com/guide/security/sec0f005981a/web (Apple Platform Security, via search summary; page rate-limited our fetch: card numbers are not stored on the device; a Device Account Number plus a one-time dynamic security code is used instead)
